title: EU: GDPR Article 17 erasure request
checklist: Replace every [PLACEHOLDER] in brackets with your own details.
Confirm you are the data subject depicted, or authorised in writing to act for them.
Find the platform's Data Protection Officer contact or privacy request form in its privacy policy.
Attach the VeriLoop evidence bundle (bundle.zip) and the signed audit PDF; keep screenshots with URL, date and time.
Only send identity documents if the controller has reasonable doubts about your identity and asks for them (Art. 12(6)).
Diary the one-month response deadline (Art. 12(3)); note the date you sent the request.
Have a lawyer verify the cited provisions before filing. VeriLoop never sends this draft.
filing_instructions: Send the request to the controller's DPO or through its privacy request form, by a channel that gives you a timestamped copy.
The controller must respond without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt; it may extend by two further months for complex requests, telling you why (Art. 12(3)).
If the controller refuses or does not answer, you can lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in your Member State of residence or work (Art. 77).

Separately, very large and other online platforms in the EU must offer a notice-and-action mechanism for allegedly illegal content (Digital Services Act, Art. 16); you can submit the same evidence there.
